title: Architecture review: KV cache fallback & routing (notes)
content:
Meeting: Architecture review — KV cache fallback & routing
Date: 2026-03-10
Attendees: Aisha Khan (owner), Jared Miller, Sofia Patel, Marco Ruiz, Emily Chen, Lina Gomez
Duration: 60m
Purpose: Review proposed RFC for KV cache sharding and discuss fallback routing behavior for cache misses, degraded nodes, and cross-region fallbacks. Reach consensus on the recommended approach and list action items for implementation and follow-ups.

Summary:
- Reviewed RFC-142 (kv-cache sharding) and three follow-up implementations notes. The core ask: ensure robust, low-latency fallbacks when a shard/node is unavailable while preserving SLOs and minimizing request amplification.
- Agreement on a two-tier fallback routing approach: local shard fallback -> intra-region replica -> cross-region fallback with degraded QoS.
- Decided to standardize a failure classification and signal set that the routing layer and runtime expose to the control plane for observability and automated rollbacks.

Key decisions made:
1) Fallback hierarchy (accepted)
   - Primary: local shard (same host or same rack) if available and healthy.
   - Secondary: intra-region replica (same model variant, warmed KV) when local shard returns transient errors or eviction thresholds exceeded.
   - Tertiary: cross-region fallback only for requests with relaxed latency SLOs or when explicitly configured via route policy (default: disabled for strict latency routes).
   Rationale: minimizes tail latency and cross-region egress costs; preserves throughput for most traffic.

2) Degraded response modes (accepted)
   - Return partial response (prefix-only) vs. full re-compute: runtime exposes flags to requestors indicating "kv-miss" vs "kv-degraded"; application-level config determines whether prefix-only is acceptable.
   - For strict deterministic routes (enterprise SLAs), prefer full re-compute on fallback rather than partial responses.

3) Failure classification (accepted)
   - Define a small set of signals: CACHE_MISS, SHARD_EVICT, SHARD_UNAVAILABLE, DEGRADE_POLICY_TRIGGER, REPLICA_LAG. These signals are surfaced via tracing and metrics and encoded in the routing decision logs.

4) Consistency model & stale reads (tentative)
   - Allow stale reads from warmed replicas with an explicit TTL policy. For now, use conservative default TTL=30s for warmed KV replicas. Team to validate against quality metrics.

Alternatives considered (short):
- Broadcast fetch to multiple replicas in parallel (pros: lowest tail; cons: doubles token cost and increases load). Rejected due to cost impact and risk to throughput.
- Synchronous replication on write to all replicas (pros: strong consistency; cons: high write latency). Rejected for same reasons.
- Client-side retry with exponential backoff (pros: simple); used only as a last resort, but not primary strategy.

Performance & SLO implications:
- Expected 95th percentile latency impact when falling back to intra-region replica: +8-20ms (measured in benchmarks). Cross-region fallback can add 60-120ms depending on region pair.
- Cost implications: cross-region fallbacks increase egress and token compute; propose a routing policy flag to opt-in per route to avoid surprises.
- Observability requirements: add per-request fallback_reason tag, and per-route fallback_rate metric. SLA alerts if fallback_rate > 0.5% for strict-latency routes.

Implementation notes / design details:
- Routing layer changes: introduce a compact "fallback policy" config in route definitions (console/API) with fields: allow_cross_region (bool), max_replica_lag_ms (int), degraded_mode (prefix_only|recompute), replica_ttl_s (int).
- KV runtime: emit TTL and replica freshness metadata in the KV response headers so routing can make informed decisions without additional RTTs.
- Cache warming: pre-warm warmed replicas for hot prefixes during canary rollouts; integrate with rollout hooks.
- Tracing: add fallback_reason and chosen_fallback_level to spans. Ensure these propagate to Console and Optimize dashboards.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Q1: What threshold for REPLICA_LAG should trigger fallback to a different replica? Action: Marco to run experiments and propose threshold values by 2026-03-17.
- Q2: How to expose per-customer fallback budget in Dedicated? Needs product input. Action: Sofia to sync with Product (due 2026-03-18).
- Q3: Acceptable stale-read TTL variance across model families (LLama2 vs GPT-style). Action: Jared to run quality evals on representative prompt sets, report by 2026-03-24.

Action items (owner — due):
- Marco Ruiz — run replica-lag sensitivity tests and propose numeric thresholds (2026-03-17).
- Sofia Patel — draft product requirements for per-customer fallback budgets and console UX (2026-03-18).
- Jared Miller — evals for stale TTL impact across model families; produce short report with quality metrics (2026-03-24).
- Emily Chen — implement tracing tags for fallback_reason and push minimal metrics to observability stack (2026-03-20).
- Aisha Khan — update RFC-142 with agreed fallback policy schema and record decisions in the RFC; prepare a short tech brief for on-call team (2026-03-16).

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: Cross-region fallbacks could create large egress costs if misconfigured. Mitigation: default disabled and add guardrails in console + quota enforcement.
- Risk: Stale reads may cause silent quality regressions. Mitigation: require canary runs of degraded mode against eval suites and automated regression alerts in Optimize.

Next steps:
- Owners to deliver above action items on schedule.
- Follow-up sync in 2 weeks to review test results and finalize TTL thresholds and Console UX.
- If experiments show acceptable quality, we will stage an opt-in canary with degraded_mode=prefix_only for a low-traffic route.

Notes & references:
- Related docs: architecture-review-kv-cache-sharding-rfc-142.json (RFC), routing notes from 2026-02-26, sharding meeting 2026-03-03.
- Benchmarks referenced are synthetic microbenchmarks run on staging clusters (Jenkins job: INF-KV-heatmap-2026-03).

Prepared by: Aisha Khan
Status: in_review — adding RFC updates and test artifacts to linked_artifacts after experiments complete.
